legacyMapping: Legacy source N is displayed as v0.0.N.
historyNote: The earliest separately documented release is v0.0.3. Original creation notes and separate entries for v0.0.1–v0.0.2, v0.0.9–v0.0.13 and v0.0.18–v0.0.22 are not recoverable from this repository. The first Git import on 25 October 2026 already contained earlier development. Historical features may be replaced by later updates.

entries.title: Full-screen 3D Universe Map
changes: Reworked the Universe Map into a full-screen textured 3D view with rings, atmospheres, orbital paths, readable labels and a compass.
Added direct 3D body selection, smooth focus and camera movement, Orbits/Labels toggles and black fades when changing systems.
Removed Universe Map Size; retained search, system selection, destination locking and route planning.
Added model LOD, bounded texture uploads, closed-map render suspension and resource cleanup.

entries.title: Cinematic camera distance fix
changes: Bound cinematic camera placement using ship size and speed so shots stay wide without losing the ship.
Refresh cinematic shots before the ship crosses the maximum distance; keep ship movement and velocity untouched.

entries.title: Cinematic flybys, space speed and atmosphere flares
changes: Camera button cycles Chase, Cockpit, Orbit and Flyby – Cinematic. Removed Planet Aligned and Space Aligned orbit choices.
Cinematic shots hold fixed world positions, track the ship center and repeat ahead of its flight path with smooth camera transitions. Ship movement and velocity are preserved.
Normal space speed is capped at 50c and boosted space speed at 100c. Existing atmospheric caps, acceleration, boost duration and cooldown are unchanged.
Added smooth orange-red exit flares from 1,800m to 5,000m without nose shine, with speed and airflow response. Smoothed entry flare transitions and disabled camera shake during cinematic shots.

entries.title: High-speed ship camera fixes
changes: Camera switches now follow the moving ship instead of pulling the view toward its previous world position.
Cinematic flyby uses a moving shot when a single frame would carry the ship past the stationary camera, while slower flybys keep stationary shots.
Flyby replacement shots refresh when the ship outruns their destination.

entries.title: Planet and space orbit cameras, cinematic flyby and larger stars
changes: Added independently rotatable Planet Aligned and Space Aligned ship orbit cameras with existing wheel/pinch zoom.
Added stationary world-space cinematic flyby shots with smooth speed-adaptive repositioning and camera clearance.
Added camera choices to the existing selector and Settings Controls, preserving legacy camera shortcuts and warp restrictions.
Narrowed Settings and added mouse-wheel scrolling to the hidden-scrollbar navigation rail.
Enlarged visible star spheres in space and surface skies without changing catalog radii, orbital coordinates or existing shine scaling.

entries.title: Compact mobile settings and consistent label filters
changes: Reduced mobile header, tabs and section heights and hid the horizontal tab scrollbar.
Combined Quality settings on one page without Display, World or Map sub-tabs.
Applied label filters to locked targets as well as ordinary labels and persisted category switches on this device.

entries.title: Cyan tabbed settings menu
changes: Redesigned settings with cyan panels, category tabs, collapsible sections, styled switches and a fixed action footer.
Organized existing world, quality, menu sizing, control and audio settings without replacing their saved values or handlers.
Added linked graphics preset buttons and a keyboard control reference, with responsive mobile layouts.
Corrected switch thumb alignment in both states.
Embedded Update Logs as a Settings tab with the shared header and footer.

entries.title: Earth-only day/night and balanced ambience
changes: Limited day/night background to Earth; airless bodies use other-bodies ambience at every altitude.
Used reentry background throughout gas-giant interiors and above 1000m on other atmospheric worlds.
Reduced background output to 20% of its previous level at the same settings, with a 100% default background slider for new preferences.
Raised plasma-gated wind to a clearer level without enabling continuous wind.

entries.title: Effect-gated wind and fading nighttime aurora
changes: Removed continuous altitude-triggered wind; quieter wind plays only while reentry plasma is active.
Kept background tracks looped independently of the wind effect.
Hid daytime aurora and added smooth 1.5-second fade-in and fade-out transitions at nightfall and daybreak.

entries.title: Correct background tracks and louder looped reentry wind
changes: Used the supplied horror ambience as the looped reentry background and supplied space ambience as the looped other-bodies background.
Played reentry above 1000m on all bodies, day/night below 1000m on atmospheric worlds, and other-bodies ambience below 1000m on airless worlds.
Added a louder separately looped wind layer alongside the reentry background.

entries.title: Looped altitude audio and faster surface sun glow
changes: Kept ground ambience below 1000m and used a looped reentry rumble above it on atmospheric bodies only.
Moved surface star glow to depth-tested GPU sprites, removing CPU triangle masking and raycasts when looking at the sun.

entries.title: Star rendering and environment audio
changes: Reduced star glow masking work to nearby foreground silhouettes.
Removed angular twisting from the ship-aligned reentry flare.
Added six environment background tracks with volume controls for ambience, weather, airflow, engine and individual effects.
Saved audio preferences and stopped background audio when the game loses focus.

entries.title: Precise nose alignment and instant world-space warp fog
changes: Anchored flare and shine directly to the authored ship nose instead of the camera subject center or bounding box.
Kept the flare on the visible model centerline while allowing shine to face the camera through every direction.
Showed the complete interstellar tunnel immediately and added fixed world-space glowing fog layers to cover its distant edge.

entries.title: Centered entry shine and brighter warp travel
changes: Centered entry flare and shine on the authored ship nose, with horizontal camera-facing shine and translucent plasma below 3600 m.
Scaled stellar shine with apparent star size and distance.
Made warps last 10 seconds and brightened the Milky Way tunnel, stars and neon rim with white entry and exit fades.

entries.title: Curved Milky Way warp and precise stellar shine
changes: Used a glowing sun inside bodies and the supplied star shine in space, with exact ship and ring occlusion instead of bounding boxes.
Wrapped the Milky Way continuously around a curved tunnel and aligned the ship and chase camera to its tangent.
Restored blue warp lines below 20 percent, above 80 percent and during same-system warps.
Centered entry flames using the unrotated flight model and placed a wider ship-facing shine at the cone tip.
Extended the globe flight band from 4000 m to 6500 m, giving 2500 m before space.

entries.title: Skybox-only warp and ship-aligned entry flames
changes: Removed glowing sticks and filaments from the warp tunnel, leaving the wrapped current skybox and its glow.
Limited entry flames to inward travel and disabled them while taking off.
Aligned symmetric flames and the forward-offset shine to ship pitch, yaw and roll, with orange, red, yellow and white colors.
Added a separate four-point color-tinted star shine in space.

entries.title: Skybox warp, staged reentry and stellar shines
changes: Replaced tunnel circles with stretched current-system skybox textures, flowing cyan and violet filaments, and fast light streaks.
Added animated ground-facing reentry flares and the supplied horizontal shine, with gradual brightness and size changes during entry and exit.
Made the globe atmosphere glow around its curved silhouette.
Replaced the old layered star shines with the supplied eight-point shine, tinted by each star color.
Raised the active space boost limit from 100c to 200c while retaining the normal 100c limit.

entries.title: Enclosed vortex tunnel and taller aurora rays
changes: Extended the visibly lit aurora rays beyond 250 m by lengthening the veil and softening its upper fade, while preserving Center Station ovals and arc animation.
Remade the tunnel with opaque blue/violet vortex walls, cyan/white filaments, fast streaks and a glowing closed far portal using the supplied image as reference.
Excluded exterior planets, sky, stars and glare from the tunnel render pass, with exception-safe restoration after rendering.
Hid world labels and the target reticle only during the tunnel phase, restoring them after exit or cancellation.
Matched the enclosed vortex and foreground ship drawing in Canvas compatibility mode; retained pooled corridor geometry and lower graphics budgets.

entries.title: Nearby warp protection, world corridor and Center aurora
changes: Rejected warp both near the departure body and when already close to the selected destination. Rechecked before confirmation and payment, including saved viewpoint travel.
Hid the minimap toggle when no usable solid-body minimap is available.
Capped every warp at ten seconds while retaining seven-second local journeys.

Replaced the camera-attached tunnel with a ship-transit corridor using a fixed journey axis, fast travel and four recycled world sections with white neon ribs and edges. Updated compatibility projection.
Selected chase camera for warp and locked camera/free/orbit mode changes until completion or cancellation.

Remade the aurora above Center Station as three animated wavy ovals that gradually open into arcs, with green, cyan, blue and magenta bands inspired by the supplied image. Retained pooled textures and geometry.

entries.title: Soft natural aurora veils
changes: Reworked aurora appearance using NASA ground-photo and aurora references: green-dominant light, subtle pink/violet accents, uneven fine rays and soft upper tails.
Replaced repeating sine stripes with a seeded translucent veil texture whose four edges fade fully away.
Separated the three gently curved curtains so they no longer intersect as bright flat panels. Retained the compact vertical height near 4 km.
Shared the same aurora artwork between WebGL and Canvas compatibility rendering, with slow deformation and brightness changes.
Generated the 512 × 128 texture once and reused the texture, canvas and bounded geometry during animation.

entries.title: Aurora curtains, staged interstellar warp and distant villages
changes: Replaced circular aurora walls with three broad flowing curtains near 4000 m, reduced their vertical height and added varied green, cyan, blue, violet and pink/red palettes. Updated the compatibility renderer to match.
Centered the square map itself in its menu and corrected the CSS specificity that overrode its width and margins. Kept zoom buttons outside on the right.
Blocked warp near physical bodies before confirmation or payment, preserving velocity and funds when rejected.
Added an interstellar tunnel that opens after 20% progress, fades closed by 85% and returns to light-beam travel. Local warp retains its beam effect.
Scaled interstellar journey duration with displayed light-year distance while preserving cancellation and existing arrival behavior.

Extended village generation beyond the original 2 km area with deterministic sparse world regions, bounded descriptor caching and nearby-only loading. Preserved original village IDs, discovery, doors and removed blocks.
Limited minimap roof generation to the viewed area and reused effect geometry, with reduced streak counts on mobile and lower graphics.

entries.title: Centered map zoom controls and compact circular range
changes: Centered the + / − column in the full space between the square map and the right menu border.
Set circular minimap coverage to 86 × 86 m when stationary and 115 × 115 m while moving, with smooth interpolation at every altitude.

entries.title: Live map buildings and natural biome placement
changes: Moved + / − zoom buttons outside the square map, in a separate right-side column.
Increased movement-based circular map zoom out and capped map coverage at 1966 × 1966 m.
Scattered biome centers more widely, varied their outlines and blended across former grid boundaries while retaining the launch-area plains.
Displayed the actual biome name when selecting its icon.
Restricted Gold and Emerald deposits to open village spaces while preserving mineral identities, inventory and mined-state saves.

Added overhead roads, station buildings, village roofs and player-built blocks to both map views. Checked structure revisions every frame, refreshed changed buildings immediately and retained destroyed blocks after villages unload.
Preserved existing village identities and player edits across the biome generation change.

entries.title: Minimap zoom and navigation lock
changes: Fixed the question-mark button so clicking it again closes the map menu.
Added right-middle + and − buttons with smooth bounded map zoom.
Added Lock To Navigation to follow the blue player arrow; dragging the map unlocks following.
Added subtle circular minimap zoom out while moving and zoom in while stationary.
Kept map controls responsive while Settings pauses gameplay.

entries.title: Smooth minimaps and a nonmodal planet map
changes: Moved coordinates, altitude, biome, planet information and the icon guide into a centered map menu, leaving a smaller circular HUD map and a bottom-right question-mark button.
Added a square 96 × 96 m map that pans with mouse or touch, keeps one terrain raster, marks Center Station at the edge and shows place names when selected. Panning does not generate gameplay terrain.
Kept the map menu nonmodal so gameplay, Settings, Account and other visible controls remain usable. Added an X close button and map-click toggle.
Avoided guest notices and right-side flight/walking controls at different minimap sizes, moving the HUD left when necessary.
Rendered map heading and positions every frame and scrolled cached terrain continuously in world coordinates.
Updated enabled shadows every rendered frame on PC and mobile, retained existing map resolutions and moved the shadow light with its stabilized target. Scene-caster discovery remains cached.

entries.title: Compact planet minimap and world updates
changes: Added a compact circular planet minimap beside Global Chat with direction labels, player heading, XYZ, altitude, current biome, planet preview and Center Station distance and edge arrow. Added landmarks for villages, trade and craft centers, launch pads, towers and biomes.
Added Minimap Menu Size in Settings and placement below the top controls with guest banner clearance. Hidden the map in space and gas interiors.
Expanded Earth aurora around 4,000m for ground and globe views. Extended wind-driven clouds across multiple terrain chunks using the existing mesh pool.
Limited ship speed to 100c, including boost.
Added a single gray ring to Quaoar and Haumea and icy blue rings to Proxima c. Enabled harvesting alien trees.
Added developer-only total and online guest counts and replaced username deletion confirmation with a checkbox tied to the selected account UID. Requires the account maintenance SQL.

Prepared a SQL migration to remove unverified email registrations after five hours on the next minute tick, protecting verified, recent, anonymous, phone, OAuth and developer accounts. Live database installation is separate.

entries.title: Corrected globe motion, streamed clouds and alien scenery
changes: Corrected globe travel direction, retained the actual entry latitude and carried travelled globe geography into space exit. Orbital flight now reaches 500 m/s, with a smooth cap increase from 3,500m to 4,000m.
Opened high-altitude arrivals directly in globe mode, removing the brief ground-view flash and second transition.
Used the same selected surface texture as each ordinary planet ball. Removed the forced Pacific orientation and duplicate Earth cloud overlay; the default Earth launch site sits on mapped land.
Matched non-Earth terrain and atmosphere color families to representative colors sampled from the bundled artwork.
Attached cloud ownership to generated terrain chunks. Clouds drift and fade within their chunks, despawn with unloaded terrain and reuse a fixed mesh pool on newly generated terrain.
Added low-poly alien trees to exoplanet and simulated-planet scenery batches without adding separate tree draw calls or changing resource rewards.
Replaced the first-person shadow caster with one capsule, preserving the Global Shadow setting.
Changed update-log titles and entries to neutral release wording such as Added and Fixed.

entries.title: Body-colored atmospheres and clearer moving globes
changes: Matched sky, fog, clouds and orbital rim colors per world, including Mars. Added artistic atmospheres for Io, TRAPPIST-1 e/f/g and simulated solid worlds.
Covered lower terrain and clouds with dense altitude fog before the black-covered globe swap. Globe surfaces use their own bundled textures without ground fog or full-disk transparent haze.

Added silhouette-only atmospheric glow, independent wind-driven clouds composited into the opaque globe and slow reversible surface movement based on ship travel. Earth daylight pauses in globe mode and space.
Clipped high-speed white wing trails once at each tail instead of folding old endpoints. Atmospheric exits leave camera clearance outside the ordinary planet ball.
Hide both Land buttons when landing is unavailable; preserve the 800m guard. Removed the free-camera plus/minus buttons while retaining sliders, wheel and keyboard controls.
Added bounded textured globe rendering for the 2D fallback and PC/mobile regression coverage. Native GPU appearance and physical-device frame rates remain unverified.

entries.title: Close Earth horizon and hidden terrain swaps
changes: Added a separate close Earth view with a blue atmospheric limb and Earth ocean/continent texture, leaving normal space planet materials unchanged.
Replaced the terrain/globe dissolve with a short black-screen fade above 4,000m and on return below 3,900m. No globe or backing sphere is shown from the ground.
Extended distant ground to a 60km radius with one mesh under 2,500 vertices, preserving detailed terrain and scenery budgets.

entries.title: Fixed glowing planets and camera-following clouds
changes: Made atmospheric haze follow star lighting and limited its radiance to the existing lit surface brightness, preventing planets from self-glowing in space.
Removed camera/player offsets from cloud positions. Clouds keep fixed world coordinates and drift only with wind.
Replaced the compatibility renderer’s screen-following Earth clouds with the same projected world-space cloud positions, keeping day/night tint and weather opacity.

entries.title: Unified atmospheric fog and the planet transition
changes: Made the globe and opaque ground shell obey the same distance fog as terrain, so they cannot bypass fog layers.
Added shared spherical atmospheric extinction and haze to surface and space planet rendering. Lower atmosphere remains visible when looking downward, even after the overhead sky darkens.
Replaced the early black fog tint and abrupt horizon clearing with continuous altitude-dependent fog ranges and a horizon that fades with the 4,000–5,000m terrain transition.
Removed the unfogged legacy atmosphere halo and matched haze colors, weather density and physical scale across local and space rendering. Mobile uses fewer atmospheric samples.

entries.title: Fixed the nearby Earth transition and intensified reentry
changes: Moved the terrain-to-planet blend to 4,000–5,000m while keeping the sky fade complete by 3,000m.
Enlarged the near-planet horizon and matched the space boundary so Earth remains close at atmospheric exit. An opaque ground shell seals terrain gaps during the blend.
Intensified airflow-facing plasma, added a compressed bow shock on desktop Ultra/Ultra+, lengthened fiery streaks and added turbulent ember movement. Low/Medium and mobile retain bounded effects.
Made reentry shake roughly four times stronger on PC, with stronger mobile shake, while retaining smooth fades and independent camera rotation and zoom.

entries.title: Fixed loading stuck at zero
changes: Let Guest and successful login continue loading immediately while slow account connection checks finish independently. Late account responses cannot replace the selected mode.
Show manifest loading progress immediately and display a Retry button if the loader itself cannot load, without clearing saved progress.

entries.title: Extended atmospheres and improved reentry
changes: Extended atmospheric flight to 5,000m, faded the sky by 3,000m and blended terrain into a spherical planet visible from 4,000m.
Set entry speed to 50 m/s and the upper atmosphere cap to 100 m/s, with a 450 m/s lower maximum and smooth cap transitions. Landing still requires descending below 800m.
Added orange-red airflow-facing heat shields, animated plasma, sparks and fiery streaks. Reentry peaks at 1,500–1,000m, fades to 800m and causes no damage.
Smoothed reentry and weaker ascent shake across all ship cameras, preserving rotation and zoom.
Added subtle heat distortion on High and above, richer Ultra/Ultra+ glow, bounded mobile particle budgets and preserved white space wing trails.

entries.title: Improved graphics and atmospheric flight
changes: Added 2,500m solid-world atmospheres, a 200 m/s upper band and a 450 m/s lower maximum with smooth cap transitions. Entry and exit retain control and momentum.
Added airflow-facing plasma, wind and subtle camera shake. Plasma peaks at 1,500–1,000m, fades to 800m and stays off below it. Exit effects are weaker, and reentry causes no damage.
Require atmospheric ships to descend below 800m before Land can engage. Airless landing remains available.
Added white wingtip trails in space, longer and brighter while boosting, with an independent saved Settings toggle. The ship model is unchanged.
Added planet micro-relief, sharper map sampling, soft cloud billows, star twinkle, richer black-hole bands and Ultra highlight/shadow improvements, with bounded mobile/Low budgets.

entries.title: Made menus compact and fixed portrait controls
changes: Added separate Menu Size settings for Account, Party, Global Chat, Daily Rewards, Update Logs and Universe Map, with smaller defaults and saved device preferences.
Separated Run Button Size from Jump Button Size, matched the Gift and Global Chat icons, and spaced Guest, Continue and sign-in actions.
Gave portrait mode compact HUD and separate steering, thrust and speed-gauge areas, and refresh the canvas after orientation/fullscreen/viewport changes.

entries.title: Improved guest menus, tutorial saves and daily supplies
changes: Save fully completed tutorials and retry interrupted account syncs. Skip leaves the tutorial available for next time. Guest tutorial preferences are remembered on this device.
Moved the Guest label below the top-right buttons and kept the account button icon-only. Guest account, friends and reward menus explain each feature and close with an X.
Added public Online/Offline status and refreshed player profiles, plus Guest Mode help.
Moved Daily Rewards to a gift icon left of Global Chat, with a ready badge and one message sound per available daily reward.
Centered and compacted the reward menu, added currency/item icons, and added building supplies throughout the week, including 64 TNT on Day 7. Server claims remain atomic and safe to retry.

entries.title: Added guest play, a beginner guide and account rewards
changes: Added Play as Guest. Guests can explore, fly, land, mine, craft and sell with temporary progress, read Global Chat and view public profiles. Signing in loads account progress without refreshing.

Added a short PC and mobile tutorial, a Skip option, Replay Tutorial in Settings and optional beginner tips. Account tutorial completion is saved; guest completion lasts only for the current page session.
Added daily rewards from 100 FP to 500 FP, with 10 RC on Day 7. The cycle repeats after seven claims and refreshes at midnight UTC.
New accounts receive a one-time welcome gift of 250 FP and 5 RC. Existing accounts keep their balances and do not receive this new-account gift.
Added discovery marks to Universe Map and aggregate player statistics to the developer menu.
Reduced startup asset preloading and stopped hidden Universe Map thumbnails from requesting textures. All five graphics modes and existing world effects remain available.

entries.title: Fixed graphics choices and mining sign-in interruptions
changes: Removed screen-edge labels for locked destinations. Their normal labels still appear when they are in view.
Added a visible Graphics quality dropdown with Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Ultra+. Older cached page layouts are repaired when the current game loads.
Stopped inventory validation and connection errors from reopening the sign-in screen. Unsaved changes stay pending, and real account/session errors still require sign-in.
Prepared a server catalogue update for every current solid body and item. Cloud saves from newer bodies still need that database update applied.

entries.title: Improved graphics, fog and space navigation
changes: Added Ultra and Ultra+ with denser scenery, more clouds and stars, higher resolution budgets, sharper images and higher-quality shadows.
Fixed empty-space clicks locking invisible bodies.
Made airless-world fog dark gray and based its fade on distance so it stays steady while looking around.
Added a 100 RC confirmation before entering Free Camera. Canceling does not spend anything.
Fixed system-to-system warp prices at 1000 FP plus 5–10 RC depending on the destination’s distance from Sol, including repeat visits. Earth return stays free.
Made Settings the only menu that pauses the simulation. Other menus and confirmations keep the world running.
Kept the locked destination label visible across systems, with a screen-edge marker when needed and distance in Ly. Intersystem bearings and distances follow the schematic game map.

entries.title: Fixed villages, ship collisions and item sounds
changes: Added a village within a short walk of the launch pad and kept existing village changes saved.
Removed the repeated explosion sound on obstacle contact. The ship now guides itself to nearby clear ground.
Fixed held resources turning with the world instead of staying in the same position in my hand.
Replaced the TNT fuse hiss with a short beep every second before the explosion.
Added TNT damage to ships and a replacement at the current world’s launch pad, while keeping on-foot players in place.
Matched the launch tower’s collision to its shaft, platforms and arm.
Stopped menu opening and button clicks from playing the same UI sound twice.

entries.title: Polished the release and added phone notification support
changes: Centered and cleaned up Update Logs on phones and computers.
Added distance fog to hide terrain edges on airless worlds.
Fixed the unnecessary exploration error in the account menu.
Removed saved places from More. Entering free camera now costs 100 RC.
Added separate phone notification settings: global chat is off by default; party chats and friend requests are on.
Added a pending friend-request count and message-style request sounds. Closed-game notifications require the push backend and browser permission.

entries.title: Update history, full game screenshots and legacy cleanup
changes: Added the Update Logs menu with recoverable release history and consistent semantic version labels.
Screenshots now capture the game viewport with HUD, controls, chat and open menus.
Removed legacy installation overlays and generated asteroid/hash labels across world, sky and map paths.
Corrected the HTML entrypoint still loading the legacy v0.0.100 boot module; startup now reads fresh release metadata and imports the matching game revision.

entries.title: v0.0.59 — pools, weather and connected roads
changes: Pools start empty and accumulate slowly, with clipped block/preview footprints and stable pool identities. Grass foley is softer; rain/snow blend across biome borders, including storms, with gusts and uneven lightning followed by thunder. Shared terrain-following roads connect the smaller 16 m pad, Earth shops, and village centers; village approaches meet doorsteps, and scenery avoids roads. Existing village edits remain saved.

entries.title: v0.0.58 — World weather, medium biomes and bounded puddle effects
changes: Rain, snow and precipitation impacts now occupy fixed world cells around the player/ship. Native graphics renders reusable scene geometry with depth testing and fog; compatibility graphics projects the same time-driven world positions. Camera rotation, zoom and orbit no longer drive particle motion or weather location. Weather remains bounded to nearby cells and stops above the cloud ceiling.

entries.title: v0.0.57 — Orbit, biome weather, map cost and gameplay audio
changes: SunRays is removed from settings, storage writes, the client module graph and source manifest; its module is deleted. The older stellar-glare streaks are also removed while the normal stellar glow remains. Space subject-orbit uses a stable world-up frame instead of changing to a nearby planet's surface normal. Orbit dragging remains available during approach autopilot, mode changes clear stale gestures, and lifting one finger after a pinch hands rotation back to the remaining finger. Chase steering retains its existing behavior.

entries.title: v0.0.56 — Startup initialization race correction
changes: Initialize movement-audio state with the other initial state, and schedule the first render frame only at the end of module initialization after the ship's asynchronous load completes. Previously the module scheduled rendering, awaited ship loading, and only then initialized `wasWalkingAirborne`; a frame during that wait could throw a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError and leave the loading screen reporting Unable to start.

entries.title: v0.0.55 — Biome weather, pool geometry, shadows and surface audio
changes: All fifteen follow-up requests are represented in this update. Puddle jump effects use a reusable, depth-tested world mesh: circular rings lie on the water plane and the ring/spray footprint stays inside the pool. Reflection cube faces now represent their actual sky directions; the water shader adds a directional reflected Sun highlight. The fallback draws that highlight only where the reflected Sun ray intersects a pool. This remains a lightweight sky reflection, not a full-scene mirror.

entries.title: v0.0.54 — Weather interactions, snow materials and mobile controls
changes: Precipitation now varies its wind direction and speed, checks the uploaded ship's opaque source-part bounds, and respects roofs. Windows retain exterior rain visibility. Reliable nearby ground-impact ripples and drops replace the sparse phase-dependent effect; landing in a rain pool adds a ring and spray. Persistent randomized pool/snow records change with weather episodes, retain harvested depletion, and accumulate on exposed roof surfaces. Ground weather stays visible across a larger bounded range; torches retain a small distant beacon while expensive point lights remain local.

entries.title: v0.0.53 — Below-cloud precipitation and lightweight ground accumulation
changes: Earth rain, heavy rain and thunderstorms stop above the lowest cloud-base height (222 gameplay meters); rain/snow use terrain/pad/roof impact heights instead of the ship's contact floor. Ground hits add small splash/ripple rings. Existing atmospheric fog remains above the clouds, while rain audio and nearby precipitation stop there. Thunder flashes now illuminate the environment.

entries.title: v0.0.52 — Texture-matched Proxima atmospheres and debug window session/size
changes: Proxima b uses a golden sky/haze, and Proxima d uses a warm tan/brown sky/haze, matching the chosen surface artwork. Sky, fog, clouds, exterior atmospheric rim and fill lighting share per-body palettes; both remain landable with Earth-like cloud heights and 800m exits.

entries.title: v0.0.51 — Server-authorized nonmodal developer tools
changes: Settings → Debug Menu opens a floating, draggable window with Close, Debug Console and Developer Panel tabs. The window does not pause gameplay or shield inventory/other controls. Keyboard focus inside developer inputs clears ship movement and prevents game shortcuts. Console includes runtime errors, command feedback and live renderer/location/position/currency/inventory diagnostics, bounded to 150 messages.

entries.title: v0.0.50 — Proxima b/d atmospheres and readable gas interiors
changes: Proxima b/d use Earth-like blue skies, drifting clouds, fog, atmospheric rims and 800m gameplay exit heights while retaining solid landing. Atmospheres/terrain remain imagined game representations. Gas interiors use palettes sampled from each selected exterior map, including blue cores/haze for ice giants and Proxima c, brighter diffuse ship lighting, and up to 12 soft animated gas-cloud sprites (4/8/12 by quality). The Canvas fallback shares palettes and world-space cloud motion. Core collision and gas exit rules are unchanged.

entries.title: v0.0.49 — Restore direction-steered Chase camera / Proxima landing rules
changes: Chase uses the original camera quaternion and offset again, preserving pitch/yaw/roll and parked crew look rather than forcing a look-at rotation. Orbit retains its ship-centered independent rotation and zoom. Proxima c is represented as a non-landable gas giant; Proxima b and d remain solid landable worlds. Old landed Proxima c saves safely migrate to gas entry.

entries.title: v0.0.48 — Ship-centered orbit camera / Planet X gas world
changes: Zoomable camera mode now orbits the uploaded ship’s visual bounding-box center, with a level horizon, clamped vertical orbit and 6–120m zoom. Mouse/touch drag rotates the view independently of the ship, right-drag is supported without the browser menu, and existing wheel/pinch/zoom buttons change orbit distance. The ship stays centered after surface-ground clearance adjustment and in chase view. Cockpit and on-foot controls are preserved.

entries.title: v0.0.47 — My Roblox texture selections and added worlds
changes: All 46 supplied IDs map to locally bundled public Roblox preview PNGs. Original asset delivery returned authentication errors; these images are explicitly preview-resolution copies (up to 420px wide), with their source IDs, dimensions and SHA-256 hashes retained in `roblox-texture-assets.js` and `assets/roblox/texture-download-report.json`. Existing full-size maps remain bundled as historical fallback assets. The Moon selection is a transparent cube-cross atlas: face-local cube-sphere UVs prevent the empty corners appearing as black surface patches, and Canvas/atlas thumbnails use an occupied face.

entries.title: v0.0.46 — Mobile building and camera frame cost
changes: Building sync retains unchanged special-block meshes, crafting-hall geometry and existing solid-block instance buffers. Player solid blocks now share material batches with village blocks; capacity grows only when needed. Door state changes replace only the door, while connected glass refreshes only changed adjacency. A spatial picking grid narrows aiming/interactions to nearby blocks instead of testing every instance in the visible world. Preview aiming is skipped without a block/shovel equipped; ground probes reuse scratch vectors. Torch candidates are cached and nearest-light selection runs at most about seven times a second. Canvas compatibility graphics now render/cull actual instance transforms.

entries.title: v0.0.45 — Upright landing and warp cockpit
changes: The new ship parks nose-up again, matching its upright liftoff and guided descent. Its model-specific 4.23m contact offset keeps the two tail nozzles just above the ground; cockpit and exhaust transforms follow the parked pose, and on-foot collision follows the upright footprint. Confirmed/paid warp switches immediately to the actual 3D cockpit; cancellation preserves the camera. Labels are hidden when any sampled part of their on-screen rectangle overlaps opaque cockpit geometry, including back faces visible from inside; transparent windows remain clear. This check applies independently of celestial-body label overlap settings.

entries.title: v0.0.44 — Uploaded TZG Player Ship
changes: Replaced the scout rocket with the supplied `TZG_Player_Ship.blend`, retaining its 124 named exterior/interior parts, UVs, six packed textures, tinted glass, luminous displays and cyan engine/cabin lights. The static mesh uses eleven material batches (4,812 triangles). The original Blender file and deterministic export script are retained under `assets/blender/`. Twin gameplay exhaust emitters align with the two rear nozzles; the static model contains no baked flames. Parked and airborne orientations match; the pilot camera sits inside the actual 3D cockpit, and on-foot collision covers the wider hull/wings while preserving a clear exit and boarding access. Compatibility graphics retain material colors; full textures and lighting use WebGL.

entries.title: v0.0.43 — Tool tap double-activation fix
changes: Touch duplicate suppression now follows pointer IDs, tap position and button identity through inventory/hotbar rerenders, including delayed clicks targeted at replacement buttons or ancestors. Touch click events with zero detail are suppressed too. Mouse, pen, keyboard and programmatic activation remain available. Regression tests cover repeated equip/unequip, tool switching, modern and legacy compatibility clicks, simultaneous taps, cancelled/scrolled gestures, disabled buttons and disconnected buttons.

entries.title: v0.0.42 — Independent touch UI
changes: Each finger can tap game buttons independently while another finger holds the thumbstick or a flight control. Touch activation tracks pointer IDs, ignores scroll/cancel gestures and suppresses the duplicate native click. Inventory is non-modal for movement input and opening/closing it preserves held movement. Held controls reject pointer takeover; an existing camera drag keeps its original pointer. Mouse and keyboard activation remain native.

entries.title: v0.0.41 — Browser right-click interruption
changes: Right/middle mouse-down clears held input and cannot start a camera drag. Opening a context menu also releases keys and cancels any captured drag, even without window blur. Native context menus are blocked over the running game view/HUD so they cannot interrupt its canvas; text fields and links retain their normal menus.

entries.title: v0.0.40 — PC focus and ship steering
changes: Keyboard input clears on tab/window focus loss, page hiding and page exits; stale auto-repeat events cannot restart a released key. Captured key-up handlers release multi-key combinations independently. A saved 0.25–3× Ship rotation speed slider is separate from look sensitivity. Space and body flight share normalized rotation rates, slowing default space steering and speeding up body steering. Post-processing uses a single fullscreen triangle, bounded depth/edge sampling, explicit framebuffer clearing, a minimized-window guard and a direct-render fallback on framebuffer failure.

entries.title: v0.0.39 — Growing upper atmosphere opening
changes: The opening starts wider above the cloud deck, then continuously expands through the remaining ascent. It retains 24% of the body sky tint instead of becoming pure black. Expansion stays strictly above the horizon; lower sky colors, fog and the cloud layer remain unchanged.

entries.title: v0.0.38 — Fog and upper sky
changes: Fog keeps its normal body/weather distance above the cloud deck. Space and stars appear only in a small, smoothly blended cap overhead; the lower sky and horizon keep their atmospheric colors. Earth weather fog remains visible at high altitude while precipitation still fades above the cloud layer.

entries.title: v0.0.37 — Atmospheres, light, glass and settlements
changes: Sound effects and rain now use Web Audio buffers, pause immediately on blur/hidden/page exit and resume ambient audio only in the foreground. Touching glass blocks omit their shared faces. Placed torches emit wider omnidirectional light; held torches illuminate nearby terrain. Cloud decks stay at a fixed world height so rockets can cross them; upper atmosphere fades toward space, with fades on body entry and exit. Each landable body has two rare deterministic village sites within 1000 m of the launch station, with spaced houses and roads built from recoverable blocks. Village discovery, open doors and TNT/shovel destruction persist in compact saves; nearby village cubes render in batches.

entries.title: v0.0.36 — Wood building blocks and cutting audio
changes: Craft 1 LogBlock or 4 WoodPlanks from 1 TreeLog, or buy 64 for 1000 FP. Both support placement, collisions, shovel recovery, saved worlds and first-person holding. LogBlock has bark sides and ringed end grain; WoodPlanks has plank seams and grain. TreeLog now uses a solid capped wooden log model in hand. Saw hits and tree felling have dedicated original sounds, separate from mineral impacts.

entries.title: v0.0.35 — Saws and TreeLogs
changes: Craft or buy Iron, Steel and Diamond Saws (25/50/100 damage). Equip a saw and click a tree trunk within 6 m. Trees have 100 HP and drop 4–8 TreeLogs; logs sell for 10 FP + 1 RC each and craft upgraded saws. Trees retain damage/removal through saves and terrain streaming; selling all resource cargo resets trees and minerals together. Centered saw/log inventory images and solid first-person saw models included.

entries.title: v0.0.34 — Body flight minimum
changes: Body entry starts at 5 m/s. Airborne body flight cannot stop or boost, and decreasing speed bottoms out at 5 m/s. Launch ramps from 5 to 40 m/s; landing still parks the ship at zero.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 33
changes: Version 33 adds P Warp, B Boost, Tab Settings and X Stop without a B/brake conflict. Crafting, trading and inventory keep the simulation running while movement input stays blocked. Airborne planet entry transforms the incoming space orientation into the local surface frame, sharing the forward-axis model/thrust convention. The five-second launch countdown leads into a four-second smooth 1–40 m/s ramp with steering available; decrease/Stop can interrupt the ramp. Landing descends faster and fully zeros both velocity vectors, retained speed and throttle on touchdown, with an exact parked position hold. Legacy airborne saves convert their old ship axis. Free camera and stable orbit camera stabilize against local planet up near surfaces with a bounded pitch.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 32
changes: Version 32 maps PC spacecraft inputs to the on-screen buttons: held Space increases retained thrust speed, Left Ctrl decreases it, W/S pitch down/up, A/D turn left/right, and Q/E roll left/right. E only opens trade/crafting or interacts with blocks while on foot. Walking and free-camera movement retain their existing controls.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 31
changes: Version 31 replaces the full-screen blue warp frame with a nonblocking destination title/subtitle and a smoothly animated progress bar directly above the boost bar, plus a left-hand Warp button opposite Boost. Confirmation/payment share the ship-position quote: non-Earth local routes cost 50–300 FP across 0–50 AU of game distance; cross-system routes cost 150–1000 FP plus 5 RC across 0–200 AU of normalized game-route distance. Separate system scenes have deterministic illustrative pricing anchors, not measured interstellar coordinates. Earth remains free. Physical star contact uses swept collision and restarts at Earth while preserving cargo/currency. Settings now includes Refresh Game, which saves then reloads the page.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 30
changes: Version 30 keeps door leaves inside their cell when opened or closed, so one-block-wide, two-block-tall entrances work. Gas interiors now use the space rocket orientation and forward thrust axis, reset cockpit/orbit state on entry, and render aligned exhaust. TNT can be crafted (2 sulfur + 1 iron) or bought (180 FP), placed, and ignited by clicking with a held torch within 5 m. A persisted four-second flashing fuse triggers a 6 m blast: nearby placed blocks and unsupported attachments return once to inventory, the fired TNT is consumed, nearby TNT chains after 0.6 s, and minerals take distance-based damage with depleted minerals collected. Blast visuals and audio are bounded; terrain, buildings and ships are preserved. All crafted building items have right-hand first-person meshes; pickaxes, minerals and shovels retain their dedicated models.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 29
changes: Version 29 adds a craftable two-cell Door (2 iron + 1 quartz or 120 FP), screen-tap/E toggling within 5 m, saved door state, physical open/closed collision and blocked-swing guards. Gas exits are 340–480 m radially from the core; core contact restarts at Earth without clearing inventory, and the interior Return to Earth shortcut is removed. Look sensitivity now reaches 6×. Low/Medium/High visibly change cloud count, streamed decoration budgets, resolution and effect passes; mobile budgets stay capped. Space uses brighter neutral fill. Planet Labels Mode saves Overlap or Collision Check (default), with foreground-body occlusion on both space and surface skies. More no longer lists the four legacy panel shortcuts.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 28
changes: Version 28 makes ladders attach flush to a solid block side and rejects floor/unsupported placement. Torches can stand on terrain/block tops or lean outward from a supporting wall. Mount IDs/faces persist; removing a support refunds attached items, and legacy unsupported ladders are returned to inventory. Glass is listed as Glass Block and retains black color/0.5 opacity. Gas cores use unlit bright materials with a glow halo; gas exits are radial distance thresholds, with core-distance HUD instead of altitude. Venus/Mars/Titan fog now respects terrain generation boundaries, and twelve low-cost cloud meshes animate with body-specific wind/tint/density on atmospheric bodies. The fallback renderer also animates clouds and brightens gas cores. Tests cover mount geometry, rejection without item loss, saved attachments/refunds, radial exits and cloud/fog behavior. Native GPU/mobile lighting performance remains unmeasured.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 27
changes: Version 27 adds climbable ladder segments, placeable emissive torches with four nearby pooled lights, and black glass with 0.5 opacity. These use the existing crafting, inventory, placement and shovel-recovery save path. Placement previews use 0.3 opacity (0.7 transparency). Mobile inventory/crafting/trade panels are limited to 430px / 76vw. The craft counter faces its eastbound connecting road. Rain particles stop at roofs and are occluded by solid blocks/glass and buildings; ladders and torches are not roofs. On-foot gravity and jump impulse vary by body. The pad radius is 12m; minerals are moved outside its footprint and clear the nearby supported Pad 01 sign board. Tests cover climbing, light/glass state, recipes/save/refunds, different-gravity jumps, shelter, pad clearance, alignment and existing systems. Browser preview uses compatibility graphics; native GPU lighting and a physical phone remain unmeasured.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 26
changes: Version 26 fixes jumping onto placed blocks. Jump height now clears a one-metre block with margin; airborne movement can cross onto block tops instead of being rejected by the ground step limit. Support and wall footprints agree, landings stay on block tops, and overhead blocks stop upward head motion. Walking/running remain 4/8 m/s. Regression coverage includes one-block jumps, higher stacked blocks, standing, stepping off, ceilings and held-jump behavior.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 25
changes: Version 25 adds Earth distance fog that ends before the nearest streamed terrain edge; a persisted terrain-size setting selects 288–864m across (9–81 chunks). It retains the mobile tree budget. Inventory now only contains search, totals, close and scrollable item/name/stack cards; world simulation and Earth time/weather continue behind it while player input remains blocked. Selling uses a separate Earth Trade window. Crafting shares the inventory panel style and uses rendered tool/concrete thumbnails. Sixteen concrete colors replace iron blocks; old carried and placed blocks migrate to gray concrete without quantity loss. One Quartz crafts five blocks; buying 64 costs 1000 FP. Colored blocks retain their color when placed, recovered, saved and restored. Earth Trade/Crafting use small building-front prompts in reach, available by E or tap. Walking/running now use 4/8 metres per second. Tests cover migration, color refunds, image availability, movement, fog/terrain bounds, and active inventory simulation. Browser QA uses the compatibility renderer; native GPU/mobile performance is unmeasured.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 24
changes: Version 24 reduces Earth scenery rendering overhead: one vertex-colored scenery mesh per nearby chunk instead of separate objects for every tree part; reusable low-poly templates; sparse mobile/Low budgets; scenery culled beyond a bounded distance and while high above ground; compatibility renderer respects hidden parent groups. Star occlusion retains per-part bounds rather than treating a whole batched chunk as a solid box. Tests cover mesh budgets, altitude culling, stable reuse, colors, and disposal. FPS on a physical phone has not been measured.

entries.title: World and gameplay update 23
changes: Version 23 adds a mineral crafting center near Earth Trade, tiered pickaxes, a shovel, and iron-block building. One Iron Ore crafts five blocks; 1000 FP buys 64. Equip blocks outside the ship to preview and place; equip the shovel and double tap the aimed block to reclaim it. Crafted items and placed blocks share the existing inventory save and cannot be sold as mined ore. Terrain uses deterministic 96m chunks with a bounded 25/49-chunk cache, including Earth trees and lunar/Martian rocks and survey equipment. Gas-giant entry uses an illustrative colored fog interior and central core; launch/land are disabled and free Return to Earth remains available. Earth gains thunderstorm weather and original synthesized rain/thunder audio.

entries.title: v0.0.17 visual and mining fixes
changes: Star glare checks opaque planets (including gas giants), ship geometry, local buildings, celestial bodies and terrain. The glare overlay also masks foreground silhouettes so the corona cannot paint over nearby objects. The loading bar stays centered independently of its spinner, which hides at completion. The title button uses the main blue HUD treatment; inventory item art is centered.

entries.title: v0.0.16 flight, atlas and menu update
changes: Right flight controls are larger: a tall Thrust control, shorter Slower control, and Stop alongside Thrust. Hold or click to change a retained forward speed command; release keeps speed and Slower stops at zero. Normal/boost limits are 150/450 m/s on surfaces and 55/320 game units per second in space. Stop clears the command and velocity. Surface forward follows the Blender rocket’s local nose (+Y after its surface rotation), with no camera dependency. Engine flames pivot exactly at the Blender bell outlet (z=1.56) in both renderers.

entries.title: v0.0.15 control and inventory fixes
changes: Cargo uses a dedicated vertically scrolling grid, preserving the scroll position while selecting and equipping. All dialogs use the main blue glass palette. The hotbar contains at most seven items including the pickaxe, with keyboard slots 1–7. The inventory toggle is centered above it.

entries.title: Reference HUD and Blender models
changes: The v14 HUD follows my four reference screenshots: two currencies centered at the top; location beneath; blue and white inventory with an on-foot hotbar; parked Launch/Leave controls; flying direction, roll, thrust and brake controls. Touch camera look uses canvas drag, and the right camera stick has no handlers or visual presence. Boost is a persistent selection beside the speed bar and applies only while moving. Inventory cannot open aboard.

entries.title: The Zero Gravity - Web — Mining Edition 8
changes: Earth retains the pilot ship on Pad 01 and adds a separate trading ship at local (18, 0.55, 13). Leave with F; the trading marker and Earth Trade button show distance. Sell from inventory while on foot within 10 m. - 48 resource types have names, colors, sale values and varying HP (60–300). Each landable body has 24 deterministic deposits with thematic mineral pools. Exoplanet placements and exotic minerals are fictional game content. Deposits show world-positioned name labels, a bar and current/max HP within 48 m on foot. - Pickaxe is slot 1. Click/tap a visible deposit or aim and press R / Swing. Reach is 6 m, each hit deals 25 HP, with a 0.42 s cooldown. Depleted nodes pay exactly one unit, remain depleted across visits/reloads, and cannot be collected twice. The first-person pickaxe animates; other selected resources appear in hand in 3D. - I / Inventory opens the cargo grid. Clicking a card or hotbar slot equips/unequips it. Separate selection buttons support multiple sale stacks, select all and deselect all. Search and name/value/quantity sorting are included. Selling a stack sells its full quantity. FP payout is each unit’s catalog value; every sold unit adds 2 RC. Partial sales retain remaining cargo and depleted nodes. When a sale empties cargo, ALL body deposits respawn and partial HP damage resets. - New accounts start with 0 FP and 0 RC. Earth deposits supply initial funding. Discovery of a new catalog body pays 5 RC once, including arrival or first physical entry; Earth is already discovered. Warping to Earth is always free, including across systems. Other normal warps cost 100 FP. Cross-system warp costs 100 FP + 5 RC. The shared Flight navigation hook also applies to distant approaches, tours and orbit transfers. Bookmarked travel charges the same fee based on its saved coordinate system. Insufficient funds cause no debit or navigation cancellation. Accepted warp charges once; cancelling an already charged warp does not refund it. Manual flight remains free. - Economy saves under `cosmic-economy-v8`: balances, inventory, claimed discoveries, damage, depleted nodes and respawn cycle. New Flight does not wipe inventory or balances, and distant rescue/reset travel charges the Earth return fee. This remains a single-player browser-local game, without multiplayer/account trading. - Kenney CC0 sound assets (Interface, Impact, Sci-fi Sounds) supply UI, equip, swing, hit, break, pickup, sale, discovery, warp, countdown, launch, landing, error and footstep effects. Settings includes a persisted effects toggle and volume. The original Google Actions library limits reuse to Google Actions, so it was excluded. Sounds unlock after a pointer/key gesture; audio pools are bounded. - Tests verify per-body deposits, HP/reach/tool/cooldown, duplicate pickup prevention, inventory equip/selection, full/partial sales, 2 RC/unit, global respawn, one-time discovery, warp charges/denial and safe persistence. Existing flight, terrain, walking and settings/UI regressions are retained. Cloud browser verification uses compatibility graphics; GPU and actual phone audio/motion require device testing.

entries.title: The Zero Gravity - Web — Walking Edition 7
changes: Parked camera look is independent from the ship. Drag the canvas or use the right thumbstick before launching; the grounded hull stays still. - Leave a parked ship with F or Leave ship. Walk in first person with WASD / the left stick, look by dragging / the right stick, run with Shift and jump with Space (mobile Jump/Run buttons). Terrain, pad steps, ship and base building contact are checked. Board within 8 m with F / Board ship. Launch is blocked while on foot, and leaving is blocked during countdown or flight. Reset returns the player aboard. - Space and airless surface skies use the photographic 360° Milky Way panorama by ESO/S. Brunier (CC BY 4.0), resized into desktop and mobile assets. The 28,000-point background overlay and fallback synthetic star dots are removed. Atmospheric worlds keep their own daytime skies. Other-system scenery remains artistic; this is an Earth-observed sky panorama reused across destinations. - UI icons are local Google Material Design SVG assets, Apache 2.0. Icon-only buttons have accessible labels. No Google font/icon CDN is required at runtime. - Tests cover parked camera separation, leave/board distance and phase guards, walking, jumping, ground/building collision and the existing manual launch/entry behavior. UI smoke checks cover parked drag, first-person controls, launch lock while walking, boarding and loaded icon elements. WebGL is mocked in this suite; browser QA uses the cloud's compatibility renderer. Physical phone sensors and GPU appearance require device testing.

entries.title: Surface launch and landing
changes: Serve `dist/` with an HTTP static server. No build step or runtime dependency download is required.

entries.title: Edition 5 — terrain, survey and compatibility
changes: Added six deterministic fictional survey systems containing 30 explicitly marked objects (six stars, eighteen planets, six moons). The catalog contains 121 destinations total. Survey system names and positions are invented, with borrowed texture artwork credited as before.

entries.title: Edition 4 — planetarium exploration
changes: The default experience now uses a free camera, inspired by the navigation patterns described in the official SpaceEngine user manual (https://spaceengine.org/manual/user-manual-0980/). The Zero Gravity - Web remains its own browser sandbox; SpaceEngine code, UI assets and branding are not included.

entries.title: Edition 3 — mobile stability, HUD ownership and image assets
changes: Settings no longer composites a blurred WebGL scene; 3D redraws are suspended while any dialog is open. Mobile canvas allocation is capped at 1.1 million pixels even at High. A tiny LRU-style image map cache keeps only two maps (Low/mobile) or three (other mobile quality settings) resident, with serial loading and disposal on eviction. Context loss saves the flight and offers a Safe graphics restart. This addresses identified resource pressure; the original crash cannot be confirmed resolved without a real device test.
